market.advice: Going into the open the tape is healthy, not fragile. SPY sits at 777.88, well clear of its 50-day at 748.06; VIX is 14.5 and falling against a 14.9 five-day average; breadth is 65% of the universe above its 50-day; and the distribution-day count is zero. Of 451 names scanned, 173 register STRONG BUY. What matters more than the index level is where the leadership is: 31 of those STRONG BUYs are financials (USB, RGA, C, MS, PNC, JPM, CFG all above 92), with refiners and midstream energy (MPC, VLO, PSX, OKE), freight and defense (EXPD, JBHT, FDX, XPO, RTX), storage and datacenter REITs (PSA, DLR) and staples (SJM, KMB) filling in behind. Meanwhile the mega-cap AI complex is still working off its excess — NVDA is 4.3% below its high with earnings in 13 days, AVGO is 13% off, MU 22% off, and AMD (17% off) and AAPL (RSI 29.6) are names TradingView now rates SELL and NEUTRAL respectively. Overnight, benign US inflation held global indices near record highs, but oil pushed higher on the US threat of an indefinite blockade of Iran with Hormuz traffic capped, and Treasury yields firmed on fresh sanctions talk. That is simultaneously the fuel under the refiner trade and the single largest tail risk to the whole tape. Plan for the session: normal position sizing, buy the un-extended breakouts and orderly pullbacks in the new leadership, let anything at RSI 80+ (NTAP, SNOW, SCHW, ABNB, GRMN, ZBRA) come back to you rather than chasing the open, and size energy for the possibility that one headline unwinds a week of gains. Utilities are the one group with essentially no leadership — a single STRONG BUY in the entire sector — so defensive rotation is going to storage REITs and staples, not to bond proxies.
